Today

If you were just charged

A charge is not a conviction. Here is what to do today.

  • Keep every paper. The citation, the bond papers and any notice of a court date all matter.
  • Write it down. While it’s fresh, note what happened, who was there and what was said.
  • Call before your first court date. Call (615) 410-7290 for a free consultation.

For family

If someone you love was arrested

You can make the first call.

Have their full name ready, and tell us what you know about the charge and any court date. At the free consultation, you can talk through what comes next. Call (615) 410-7290.

Charges

Charges Will Fraley handles

Will Fraley handles DUI, drug, theft, violent crime, sex crime, fraud, probation violation and domestic assault cases.

  • DUI

    First and second offense DUI, felony DUI and underage DUI. Also driving while suspended, reckless driving and vehicular homicide.

    DUI defense

  • Drug crimes

    Possession, use or manufacture of a dangerous drug, marijuana possession and paraphernalia charges. Distribution charges too.

    Drug crime defense

  • Theft

    Theft, robbery and burglary charges.

    Theft defense

  • Violent crimes

    Assault and battery, manslaughter, and murder or attempted murder.

    Violent crime defense

  • Sex crimes

    Accusations such as rape, sexual battery, child molestation and prostitution.

    Sex crime defense

  • Fraud

    Embezzlement, forgery, identity theft, and credit card, insurance, mail, wire and tax fraud.

    Fraud defense

  • Probation violation

    Accused of violating your probation? Will Fraley can help you answer it and get back to your life.

    Probation violation defense

  • Domestic assault

    Domestic assault charges, and related assault and aggravated assault charges.

    Domestic assault defense

The process

How a criminal case moves

  1. 01
    Step 1: The charge.

    A case starts with an arrest or a citation and a first court date. Bring every paper you received to your consultation.

  2. 02
    Step 2: The consultation.

    You tell your side. You learn, in plain terms, what the charge means and what your options are.

  3. 03
    Step 3: The review.

    Your lawyer studies the charge, the reports and the evidence, and looks for weak points in the case against you.

  4. 04
    Step 4: The options.

    Will looks for every lawful way to get the charges reduced or dismissed. Some cases are resolved by agreement; others go to trial.

  5. 05
    Step 5: Court.

    If your case goes to trial, you have a trial attorney beside you.

Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome.
